main_text.p: hibeant testes conscientiæ ipsorum annuentes atque attestantes. Perseverantiam denotant hæc verba, Consistentes sunt pedes nostri. Fines illius perseverantiæ circumscribuntur ab illis, cùm inquiunt, in portis tuis. Testimonium verò Ecclesiæ ad hæc omnia appellatur, quia illius est testificari secundum Deū, tum de portis suis (vt cum Propheta loquamur) tum de membris intra portas eius agentibus.

Ac primus quidem ille locus de perseverantia sanctorum nō temerè à piis adhibetur: quia omnes homines ad sanctitatem veram à Deo provocati & accensi in Ecclesia eius, adhuc ea cæcitate mentis & carnis infirmitate sunt, dum hic in terris vivunt & lubricū iter huius mundi premunt, vt nullo fermè negotio pedes eorum à viis quas Deus præscripsit avertantur. Probat Deus, excæcat mundus, debilitat caro, peccatum [illegible, ~2 letters]ngit, Satanas fallit, omnia denique pedibus piorum insidiari videntur quàm periculosissimè, nisi Dei manus, Ecclesiæ ars, & nostra ipsorum observatio diligentissima adversus tot mala, quæ nos infestant, concurrerint. Peregrinantes itaque pij à Domino & arduum huius vitæ iter cōtemplantes, quo ex se ipsis egredi, in Ecclesiam ingredi, & ad Deum transgredi ipsos necesse est, actionem illam spiritalem corporeis umbraculis significauerunt, cùm sibi pedes in hoc spiritali incessu & consistendi of-ficium tribuerunt. page.notes: Printed text runs from the top of the page to "siue" at the foot; "con-" is the catchword at the right. A dark stain or blot covers part of the word after "peccatum" ("tum...ngit"); the letters under it are unreadable, so I marked them as illegible. The left-hand edge shows the neighbouring page's show-through and was excluded. Handwritten marks in the top right margin were excluded. Printed "s" forms were normalised to plain s, and the italic phrases were marked. The word "pedes" (after "cùm sibi") is partly obscured by the fold in the printed line; it reads clearly enough, but the line "cùm sibi pe-des" was joined across the hyphen as printed.
